text:
Two fixes in banchi. Main moves by PR only.

1. `make hooks` disarms itself on a fresh clone. The recipe sets core.hooksPath, then runs
   `git config --worktree --unset-all core.hooksPath` on each worktree. With
   extensions.worktreeConfig off (any fresh clone; the Mac clone has it on), --worktree writes
   the shared .git/config, so the loop clears the value it just set. It still prints
   "hooks armed", because its check reads the copied files, not the config.
   Reproduced 2026-11-03 and again on main affcbb7: fresh clone, `make hooks`, then
   `git config core.hooksPath` exits 1.
   Fix the cause in the recipe: turn on extensions.worktreeConfig before the loop, or skip the
   unset for the main worktree. Then make the recipe's final check read
   `git config core.hooksPath` and fail when it is not the hooks-armed path.
   Prove it red then green in githooks-selftest (a fresh clone with worktreeConfig off).
   The cloud setup script carries a workaround (it turns worktreeConfig on first). Say in the
   report when the workaround can go.

2. Six T7 checks cannot pass in a Claude Code cloud VM (measured 2026-11-02 on main b86f621;
   9 of 10 harness tests green otherwise):
   - 4 read-only-door checks in harness/tests/t7/store_core.py chmod a folder 0555. The VM
     runs as root, and root ignores the mode.
   - 2 dual-stack bind checks need IPv6. The VM kernel has none (socket(AF_INET6) gives errno 97).
   This changes what a test proves, so bring it to the owner first, with options and a pick.
   My pick: report each as a named SKIP when euid is 0 or IPv6 is absent, counted by
   scripts/ci-skip-count.sh, never as a pass. CI is non-root with IPv6, so CI is unchanged.
